benchmark: AstraDJ local multi-room Lounge acceptance and performance

runtime.frontendMode: Vite development server; real production bundles and deployment infrastructure are not used.

methodology.queueWorkload: 3 rooms concurrently; 5 authenticated participants per room; 1 queue additions per second per room for 5 seconds; operations start at configured intervals and are flushed before report. Room lg_e62e6120d124a1ac uses 5 real Chromium/React clients; other rooms use authenticated Socket.IO clients.
methodology.warmup: No synthetic mutation warm-up is included; join and schema index initialization occur before measurement.
methodology.trace: Each queue attempt carries a UUID through the authenticated command, durable QueueEvent/outbox, queue broadcast, browser Socket.IO receipt, React queue-state application, two-requestAnimationFrame DOM marker, and server-received render acknowledgement. The marker reports the rendered revision, ordered track IDs, and canonical SHA-256 queue-state hash.
methodology.queueDriftDefinition: For each accepted mutation, the conservative bound starts at queue-command receipt and ends when the same API process receives a valid render acknowledgement from every connected client in the measured room. Each acknowledgement follows the browser DOM marker and verifies identical broadcast revision, ordered queue IDs, and canonical state hash. The bound includes acknowledgement return latency and is not the exact client render instant. The target metric is the nearest-rank P95 of complete per-mutation bounds; every attempt, including incomplete samples, is counted separately and any incomplete sample prevents acceptance.
methodology.clockMethod: Command receipt, database commit, broadcast, receipt acknowledgement, and render acknowledgement durations use performance.now() on the same API process. No server/browser or cross-process monotonic timestamps are subtracted. Browser receive-to-state-application and receive-to-render durations use performance.now() within the same page. Cross-process acknowledgement elapsed values are null unless the event originated on that API process; wall-clock stamps are informational only and never used for latency calculations.
methodology.rateLimitHandling: The benchmark uses a unique disposable database. To collect more than five segue samples per room despite the production limit of 10 playback actions/user/minute, the benchmark clears only the disposable database rate-limit counters before segue sample 16. Rate-limit throughput is not measured by this workload.
methodology.clientApplyAndRender: Browser receipt, React state application, and actual DOM completion are distinct measures. DOM completion follows a React commit and two requestAnimationFrame callbacks. Socket.IO-only clients record receipt and setImmediate state/render proxies for diagnostics only and are excluded from browser-render acceptance.
methodology.percentileMethod: Nearest-rank p50/p95/p99: sorted sample at ceil(p*n), 1-based. The queue P95 population consists only of complete, hash-valid all-client render acknowledgement upper bounds; attempted, accepted, rejected, late, complete, and incomplete counts are reported alongside it.
methodology.chatAndReconnect: One unique persisted chat message per room delivered to every currently joined socket; disconnect a listener, send a second message, reconnect/join, and verify authoritative queue snapshot plus history recovery.
methodology.clientSourceAddresses: Each room uses a distinct loopback source address (127.0.0.1 onward) so its 5 initial sockets remain below the shared per-IP connection-attempt limit; this does not model a single-NAT multi-room burst.
methodology.lifecycle: Host end command, durable ended status, and end notification count observed in the Socket.IO rooms; lifecycle and chat/reconnect checks are reported as skipped for the browser-measured room.
methodology.browserAuth: Each browser client uses an isolated context and a refresh-token cookie seeded only in the disposable Mongo database; the application restores a distinct real user session and Socket.IO authenticates normally. Contexts are opened sequentially to avoid startup bursts; all pages share one local Chromium process. Browser pages connect through Vite to the first API process; both API instances share the same Mongo database.

prdTargets.concurrentRoomDescription: handful; local acceptance uses the configured room count

queueSyncDrift.boundary: Upper bound from queue command receipt to the server receiving the last valid browser render acknowledgement. Each acknowledgement follows React state application and two requestAnimationFrame callbacks and contains the rendered DOM revision, canonical track IDs, and SHA-256 state hash. Includes acknowledgement return latency; this is conservative, not the exact client render instant.

webSocketFanout.boundary: Server command receipt to the last participant Socket.IO receipt acknowledgement observed by the same API process monotonic clock. Cross-process events without a comparable origin clock are excluded and counted as incomplete.

serverProcesses.mongoCommandMonitoring: driver command-started/succeeded/failed; aggregate by command and collection; durations use this process monotonic clock

diagnostics.limitations: CPU and event-loop telemetry is per API process; browser long-task entries are per page. This localhost benchmark does not establish production topology, network conditions, or production MongoDB contention.

samples.note: Socket/service boundary with synthetic currentTs; no audio clock or browser render measurement.

segue.disposition: Service/socket proxy only; no real media clock or browser render measurement. P95 target remains unverified even if the proxy is below 3000 ms.

lifecycle.reason: Host lifecycle coverage runs through the Socket.IO cohorts in the other concurrent rooms.

prdDisposition.queueSyncDrift: Local browser DOM render-ack upper bound for 5 browser pages in one room; all-client render drift is incomplete if any Socket.IO-only participant remains in that room. Not production-representative.
prdDisposition.webSocketFanout: Server-observed command receipt-to-client receipt acknowledgement on one API process monotonic clock; cross-process samples are not compared. Production network fan-out remains unverified.
prdDisposition.roomCapacity: Not run at the PRD 50-user design capacity.
prdDisposition.multipleRooms: 3 rooms exercised concurrently across two app processes against one local MongoDB instance.
prdDisposition.segue: Measured separately from queue event fan-out and remains unverified at the true outro-entry-to-browser-rendered boundary.
